summary: @grabcad/grabcad-shop-shared ships a postinstall beacon exfiltrating host metadata to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package publishes under the `@grabcad` scope but provides no real functionality: `index.js` exports a Proxy stub that no-ops every property access, and the package self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim'. A `postinstall` hook runs `node beacon.cjs`, and `index.js` also invokes the same `fire()` routine on require. `beacon.cjs` POSTs a JSON payload containing the package name, `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` (install path), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc` over plaintext HTTP. The combination of a scope-matching stub plus install-time and require-time reconnaissance to a non-registry, non-publisher bare-IP destination is the canonical dependency-confusion recon pattern: the stub lets a consumer build succeed silently after accidentally resolving this package instead of an internal `@grabcad` package, while the beacon discloses the victim's hostname, project path, and runtime to the operator for follow-on targeting.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
